title: Rule of Law in a Mixed Economy

content.overview: In a mixed economy the State regulates and participates in economic activity while private enterprise continues. The rule of law requires that economic regulation and public commercial action remain authorised by law, non-arbitrary and subject to review, even where wide policy discretion exists.
content.glance: Identify the regulatory or commercial power; test legal authorisation and non-arbitrariness; apply the appropriate intensity of review for economic policy without abandoning legality.
content.study: Mixed-economy administration involves licensing, price controls, public sector undertakings and regulatory agencies. Wide economic discretion is common, but it is not a zone of immunity. Article 14, directive principles of policy and sectoral statutes structure legal limits. Courts often defer on pure policy choice while intervening for illegality, procedural unfairness or patent arbitrariness. Current-law framing: ground the analysis in the Constitution and the sectoral statute. Do not treat BSA 2023 as the source of this doctrine.

sections.heading: Mixed Economy Context
sections.body: State regulation and participation coexist with private enterprise.

sections.heading: Legal Authorisation
sections.body: Every regulatory measure needs a statutory or constitutional source.

sections.heading: Non-Arbitrariness in Economic Action
sections.body: Article 14 constrains arbitrary economic regulation and state commercial conduct.

sections.heading: Intensity of Review
sections.body: Policy deference is real but not absolute; legality and fairness remain reviewable.

sections.heading: Remedies
sections.body: Writs, statutory appeals and sectoral tribunals provide enforcement routes.

examples.title: Licensing without criteria
examples.body: A licensing authority refuses a licence without stated criteria or reasons. Non-arbitrariness and legality review are engaged despite economic subject-matter.

examples.title: Policy change with fairness
examples.body: Government changes an economic policy prospectively after notice. Policy deference may apply if legality and fairness are observed.

hypotheticals.question: Do courts never review economic policy?
hypotheticals.analysis: They review legality and arbitrariness even if they defer on pure policy merits.

hypotheticals.question: Is public sector action always immune as policy?
hypotheticals.analysis: Public sector action remains subject to law and constitutional standards.

distinctions.title: Policy deference vs legality review
distinctions.left: Courts respect primary economic policy choice
distinctions.right: Courts still police jurisdiction, procedure and arbitrariness

misconceptions.correction: They review legality and arbitrariness even if they defer on pure policy merits.

misconceptions.trap: Public sector action is always immune as policy.
misconceptions.correction: Public sector action remains subject to law and constitutional standards.

cases.name: A.K. Kraipak v Union of India
cases.issue: How far do natural justice rules apply to administrative action?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Natural justice applies where fairness requires it; bias is impermissible.
cases.holding: Selection process invalidated for breach of natural justice.
cases.relevance: Authority already in the file on fair administrative procedure.

cases.name: Maneka Gandhi v Union of India
cases.facts: Passport impounded without adequate opportunity and reasons.
cases.issue: Standard of fairness for State action affecting liberty.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Procedure affecting Article 21 liberty must be fair, just and reasonable.

cases.name: Tata Cellular v Union of India
cases.issue: Limits of judicial review over administrative discretion.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Review examines illegality, irrationality and procedural impropriety, not merits as an appellate authority.
cases.holding: Classic Indian administrative review framework stated.
cases.relevance: Authority already in the file on review of commercial/administrative decisions.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a mixed-economy rule-of-law problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify regulatory/commercial power. II. Test legal authorisation. III. Apply non-arbitrariness. IV. Calibrate review intensity. V. Formulate remedy.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Source of power; legality and fairness defects; intensity of review; precise relief.

examTips: Note policy deference is not immunity.
Use Tata Cellular for review intensity in commercial contexts.
